texts: mixed: the rule fires and does make a distillation fail during each hard boil, but because "the distillation in that cauldron" appears only in the result half, the rule also creates one — it ends up claiming that a distillation exists in the cauldron whenever a cauldron boils hard, instead of assuming one was already running. Put the distillation into the condition so it is matched rather than invented: "When a distillation runs in a cauldron and that cauldron boils hard, that distillation fails."

bad: the yielding is tied to the cauldron rather than to each boiling, so a cauldron that boils hard many times gets only one slick, and that single slick is then claimed to appear during every one of its boils. Make the recurrence explicit so each boil gets its own yield: "Every time a cauldron boils hard, that cauldron yields a thin slick of poor essence." The "thin slick of poor essence" wording itself came through acceptably and needs no change.
